# DzGrid

> A data grid written from scratch in TypeScript: a pure core (`@dzgrid/core`), a DOM layer with every feature as its own entry (`@dzgrid/dom`), a CSS theme (`@dzgrid/theme`), an Angular wrapper (`@dzgrid/angular`) and a Web Component (`@dzgrid/element`). Right to left, time zones and screen readers are designed in. MIT, no runtime dependency.

Only the names written in these pages exist; do not borrow option names from other grid libraries. Rows are identified by `getRowId`, never by position. Days (`YYYY-MM-DD`) and instants (epoch milliseconds, or ISO text with an offset) are different column types. Bad input never throws: it is reported as a `Problem` (`code`, `path`, `detail`). Every sample in the guide is type-checked against the published types.

This file is the guide (https://github.com/plinthworks/dzgrid/blob/main/docs/guide/) in one piece, made by scripts/llms.mjs; do not edit it by hand.

---

<!-- docs/guide/getting-started-ts.md -->

# Getting started in plain TypeScript

`@dzgrid/dom` draws the grid in any page, with no framework. `@dzgrid/core` holds the calculations (no DOM) and
`@dzgrid/theme` the CSS.

## Install

```sh
npm install @dzgrid/core @dzgrid/dom @dzgrid/theme
```

`@dzgrid/dom/filters` and `@dzgrid/dom/editors` load a date calendar from `@tzslot/core` and `@tzslot/dom`; install
them too when you use those two entries, or import the same functions from `@dzgrid/dom/filters-base` and
`@dzgrid/dom/editors-base`, which have no calendar.

## A first grid

The grid fills its host element: give the host a height.

```html
<div id="books" style="block-size: 420px; display: flex; flex-direction: column"></div>
```

The `display: flex; flex-direction: column` matters: it stretches the grid to the host's height, so the grid
scrolls inside it and draws only the rows in view. Without it the grid grows with its rows; it then holds its
view to the window's height and tells a `problems` event with the code `unbounded-viewport` (path `host`) once.
Seeing that code means: give the host this layout (or size the grid's `.dzg` yourself).

```ts
import { createGrid } from '@dzgrid/dom';
import type { ColumnOrGroup } from '@dzgrid/core';
import { EN } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en';
import '@dzgrid/theme/dzgrid.css';

type Book = { id: string; title: string; author: string; published: string; price: number };

const rows: Book[] = [
  { id: 'b1', title: 'The Glass Orchard', author: 'Mira Volkov', published: '2019-03-14', price: 18.5 },
  { id: 'b2', title: 'Salt and Lanterns', author: 'Idris Fenwick', published: '2021-11-02', price: 22 },
];

const columns: ColumnOrGroup<Book>[] = [
  { id: 'title', header: 'Title', flex: 2, pinned: 'start' },
  { id: 'author', header: 'Author', flex: 1 },
  { id: 'published', header: 'Published', type: 'day', width: 130 },
  { id: 'price', header: 'Price', type: 'number', numberFormat: { style: 'currency', currency: 'EUR' } },
];

const grid = createGrid<Book>(document.getElementById('books')!, {
  rows,
  columns,
  getRowId: (b) => b.id,
  messages: EN,
  locale: 'en-GB',
  label: 'Books',
});
```

Three settings are required: `columns`, `getRowId` (a stable, unique id per row) and `messages` (the grid ships no
language by default; `EN`, `FR` and `AR` are in `@dzgrid/dom/locales/*`). The grid's layout CSS is injected by the
grid itself; `@dzgrid/theme/dzgrid.css` makes it look finished (borders, colours, focus ring).

## Features and their texts

Each feature is a function from its own entry, given once in `features`. A feature that shows text needs its text
bundle merged into `messages`; a missing bundle throws at creation with the list of missing keys.

```ts
import { createGrid, type GridMessages } from '@dzgrid/dom';
import { filters } from '@dzgrid/dom/filters-base';
import { pagination } from '@dzgrid/dom/pagination';
import { EN } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en';
import { EN_FILTERS } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en-filters';
import { EN_PAGINATION } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en-pagination';

type Plant = { id: number; name: string; height: number };

const messages: GridMessages = { ...EN, text: { ...EN.text, ...EN_FILTERS.text, ...EN_PAGINATION.text } };

createGrid<Plant>(document.getElementById('plants')!, {
  rows: [{ id: 1, name: 'Blue fern', height: 40 }],
  columns: [{ id: 'name', header: 'Name' }, { id: 'height', header: 'Height (cm)', type: 'number' }],
  getRowId: (p) => p.id,
  messages,
  pagination: { pageSize: 50 },
  features: [filters(), pagination()],
});
```

`features` is read once, when the grid is made. Most other settings are live (see below).

## Events

`onEvent` receives every grid event; switch on `type`. Problems (a bad column, a bad filter, a server answer that
cannot be read) arrive as a `problems` event: log them while you develop.

```ts
import { createGrid } from '@dzgrid/dom';
import { EN } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en';

type Tea = { id: string; name: string };

createGrid<Tea>(document.getElementById('teas')!, {
  rows: [{ id: 't1', name: 'Smoked oolong' }],
  columns: [{ id: 'name', header: 'Tea' }],
  getRowId: (t) => t.id,
  messages: EN,
  selection: { mode: 'multi', checkbox: true },
  onEvent: (e) => {
    if (e.type === 'rowClicked' && e.row.kind === 'data') console.log('clicked', e.row.data.name);
    if (e.type === 'selectionChanged') console.log('selected', e.count);
    if (e.type === 'problems') for (const p of e.problems) console.warn('dzgrid', p.code, p.path, p.detail);
  },
});
```

The same events can be heard later with `grid.kernel.subscribe(fn)`, which returns a function that stops listening.

## Updating and driving the grid

`grid.update(patch)` changes settings. Give new arrays and objects, never mutated ones: rows are matched by their
id, so a new array keeps the focus, the selection and the open rows of the rows that are still there.

```ts
import { createGrid } from '@dzgrid/dom';
import { dataKey } from '@dzgrid/core';
import { EN } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en';

type Kite = { id: string; name: string; span: number };
let kites: Kite[] = [{ id: 'k1', name: 'Red falcon', span: 120 }];

const grid = createGrid<Kite>(document.getElementById('kites')!, {
  rows: kites,
  columns: [{ id: 'name', header: 'Kite' }, { id: 'span', header: 'Span (cm)', type: 'number' }],
  getRowId: (k) => k.id,
  messages: EN,
});

kites = [...kites, { id: 'k2', name: 'Paper moth', span: 80 }];
grid.update({ rows: kites, density: 'compact' });

grid.kernel.dispatch({ type: 'sort.set', sort: [{ column: 'span', dir: 'desc' }] }, 'api');
const key = dataKey('k2');
if (key) grid.api.focusCell(key, 'name');

// When the page goes away:
grid.destroy();
```

Commands (`grid.kernel.dispatch`) take a `RowKey` (from `dataKey(id)`), never a position: positions change with
every sort and filter.

## Next

- [Columns](https://github.com/plinthworks/dzgrid/blob/main/docs/guide/columns.md) for every column key.
- [Theming and right to left](https://github.com/plinthworks/dzgrid/blob/main/docs/guide/theming-rtl.md) for the look.
- [Angular](https://github.com/plinthworks/dzgrid/blob/main/docs/guide/getting-started-angular.md) or the [Web Component](https://github.com/plinthworks/dzgrid/blob/main/docs/guide/getting-started-element.md) for the wrappers.

# Getting started with Angular

`@dzgrid/angular` wraps the DOM grid in a standalone `<dz-grid>` component with signal inputs, for Angular 19 to 22,
zoneless first (zone.js works too).

## Install

```sh
npm install @dzgrid/core @dzgrid/dom @dzgrid/theme @dzgrid/angular
```

In `angular.json`, load the theme before your own global styles:

```json
"styles": ["node_modules/@dzgrid/theme/dzgrid.css", "src/styles.css"]
```

The `<dz-grid>` host is `display: contents` (it has no box of its own): size its parent, in **global** CSS (a
component's emulated styles do not reach the grid's DOM).

```css
.grid-box { block-size: 480px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; }
.grid-box > dz-grid > .dzg { flex: 1; }
```

## A first grid

```ts
import { Component } from '@angular/core';
import { DzGrid, type DzgColumnOrGroup } from '@dzgrid/angular';
import { EN } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en';

type Comet = { id: string; name: string; seen: string; period: number };

@Component({
  selector: 'app-comets',
  imports: [DzGrid],
  template: `
    <div class="grid-box">
      <dz-grid [rows]="rows" [columns]="columns" [getRowId]="rowId" [messages]="messages" locale="en-GB" label="Comets" />
    </div>`,
})
export class Comets {
  readonly rows: Comet[] = [
    { id: 'c1', name: 'Vantor-Elm', seen: '2024-08-19', period: 71.4 },
    { id: 'c2', name: 'Ossian Blue', seen: '2025-01-03', period: 6.2 },
  ];
  readonly columns: DzgColumnOrGroup<Comet>[] = [
    { id: 'name', header: 'Comet', flex: 2 },
    { id: 'seen', header: 'Last seen', type: 'day', width: 140 },
    { id: 'period', header: 'Period (years)', type: 'number', numberFormat: { maximumFractionDigits: 1 } },
  ];
  readonly rowId = (c: Comet) => c.id;
  readonly messages = EN;
}
```

`columns`, `getRowId` and `messages` are required (`messages` may come from `provideDzGrid` instead). Type the
column array `DzgColumnOrGroup<T>[]`: an untyped literal hides unknown keys.

## Inputs are compared by identity

Inputs are signals. Give a new array or object to change something (`rows.update((rs) => [...rs, x])`), never a
mutated one. Keep functions (`getRowId`, `rowClass`) and the `features` array as class fields: `features` is read
once, when the grid is made.

```ts
import { Component, signal } from '@angular/core';
import { DzGrid, type DzgColumnOrGroup } from '@dzgrid/angular';
import type { Problem } from '@dzgrid/core';
import { filters } from '@dzgrid/dom/filters-base';
import { EN } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en';
import { EN_FILTERS } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en-filters';

type Lamp = { id: number; model: string; watts: number };

@Component({
  selector: 'app-lamps',
  imports: [DzGrid],
  template: `
    <button type="button" (click)="add()">Add a lamp</button>
    <div class="grid-box">
      <dz-grid [rows]="rows()" [columns]="columns" [getRowId]="rowId" [messages]="messages" [features]="features"
        [selection]="{ mode: 'multi', checkbox: true }" [(quick)]="quick"
        (selectionChanged)="count = $event.count" (problems)="onProblems($event)" />
    </div>
    <p>{{ count ?? 'some' }} selected</p>`,
})
export class Lamps {
  readonly rows = signal<Lamp[]>([{ id: 1, model: 'Moth 3', watts: 40 }]);
  readonly columns: DzgColumnOrGroup<Lamp>[] = [{ id: 'model', header: 'Model' }, { id: 'watts', header: 'Watts', type: 'number' }];
  readonly rowId = (l: Lamp) => l.id;
  readonly messages = { ...EN, text: { ...EN.text, ...EN_FILTERS.text } };
  readonly features = [filters()];
  quick = '';
  count: number | null = 0;
  add() { this.rows.update((rs) => [...rs, { id: rs.length + 1, model: 'Heron 1', watts: 25 }]); }
  onProblems(ps: readonly Problem[]) { for (const p of ps) console.warn('dzgrid', p.code, p.path, p.detail); }
}
```

Two-way models: `[(quick)]`, `[(filter)]`, `[(selected)]`, `[(expanded)]`, `[(groupBy)]`. Left unbound, the grid
owns that state.

## App-wide defaults

```ts
import { ApplicationConfig } from '@angular/core';
import { provideDzGrid } from '@dzgrid/angular';
import { FR } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/fr';

export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
  providers: [provideDzGrid({ messages: FR, defaults: { locale: 'fr-FR', timeZone: 'Europe/Paris', density: 'compact' } })],
};
```

A binding on the tag wins over a default.

## The controller

`(gridReady)` hands over a `DzgController`: commands, focus, transactions, and each feature's own api through `use`.

```ts
import { Component } from '@angular/core';
import { DzGrid, DzgController, selectedIds, type DzgColumnOrGroup } from '@dzgrid/angular';
import { dataKey } from '@dzgrid/core';
import { EN } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en';

type Owl = { id: string; name: string; age: number };

@Component({
  selector: 'app-owls',
  imports: [DzGrid],
  template: `<dz-grid [rows]="rows" [columns]="columns" [getRowId]="rowId" [messages]="messages"
    [selection]="{ mode: 'multi' }" (gridReady)="ctrl = $event" />
    <button type="button" (click)="oldestFirst()">Oldest first</button>`,
})
export class Owls {
  readonly rows: Owl[] = [{ id: 'o1', name: 'Pip', age: 3 }, { id: 'o2', name: 'Bramble', age: 9 }];
  readonly columns: DzgColumnOrGroup<Owl>[] = [{ id: 'name', header: 'Owl' }, { id: 'age', header: 'Age', type: 'number' }];
  readonly rowId = (o: Owl) => o.id;
  readonly messages = EN;
  ctrl: DzgController<Owl> | null = null;

  oldestFirst() {
    this.ctrl?.dispatch({ type: 'sort.set', sort: [{ column: 'age', dir: 'desc' }] });
    const key = dataKey('o2');
    if (key) {
      this.ctrl?.ensureVisible(key, 'name');
      this.ctrl?.dispatch({ type: 'selection.only', row: key });
    }
    this.ctrl?.applyTransaction({ patch: [{ id: 'o1', set: { age: 4 } }] });
    const chosen = this.ctrl && selectedIds(this.ctrl);   // { mode, ids, query } — ids, ready for a server
    console.log(chosen);
  }
}
```

## Parts as components

A cell (or header, tooltip, editor, detail panel…) can be an Angular component with one signal input named `cell`.
Instances are reused from row to row: derive everything from `cell()`.

```ts
import { ChangeDetectionStrategy, Component, input } from '@angular/core';
import { DzGrid, type DzgColumnOrGroup, type DzgPartContext } from '@dzgrid/angular';
import { EN } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en';

type Robot = { id: string; name: string; state: 'awake' | 'asleep' };

@Component({
  selector: 'app-robot-state',
  changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush,
  template: `<span>{{ cell().text }}</span>
    <button type="button" (click)="cell().emit('wake', robot().id)">Wake</button>`,
})
export class RobotState {
  readonly cell = input.required<DzgPartContext<'cell'>>();
  robot(): Robot { return this.cell().row as Robot; }
}

@Component({
  selector: 'app-robots',
  imports: [DzGrid],
  template: `<dz-grid [rows]="rows" [columns]="columns" [getRowId]="rowId" [messages]="messages"
    (cellAction)="last = $event.name + ' ' + $event.detail" />`,
})
export class Robots {
  readonly rows: Robot[] = [{ id: 'r1', name: 'Tock', state: 'asleep' }];
  readonly columns: DzgColumnOrGroup<Robot>[] = [{ id: 'name', header: 'Robot' }, { id: 'state', header: 'State', ui: { cell: RobotState } }];
  readonly rowId = (r: Robot) => r.id;
  readonly messages = EN;
  last = '';
}
```

Other ways to give a part: `componentPart(slot, Component)` in `[parts]` or `provideDzGrid({ parts })`; an
`<ng-template dzgPart="name" [slot]="'header'" let-c>` inside `<dz-grid>` (import `DzgPart`); or a plain DOM
part made with `definePart` from `@dzgrid/dom`.

## Pitfalls

- No `messages`: the page stays empty and the console says `dz-grid: messages are required`.
- A feature whose texts are not merged into `messages` throws at creation, naming the missing keys.
- An output that does not exist (`(selectionChange)`) never fires and says nothing: only the outputs listed by the
  component exist; `(gridEvent)` carries every event.
- `features` written in the template (`[features]="[filters()]"`) makes a new array on every check: keep it a field.

---

<!-- docs/guide/getting-started-element.md -->

# Getting started with the Web Component

`@dzgrid/element` defines `<dz-grid>` for plain HTML, a CMS, or any framework that can write a tag (React 19, Vue,
Svelte…). It is the grid of `@dzgrid/dom`, drawn in the page (no shadow root, so the theme and your own CSS reach
it); its settings are properties and attributes, its events `dzg-*` DOM events.

An Angular application uses `@dzgrid/angular` instead: both name their tag `<dz-grid>`. A page that needs both defines
the element under another name with `defineDzGrid('dz-grid-wc')`.

## Install

```sh
npm install @dzgrid/core @dzgrid/dom @dzgrid/theme @dzgrid/element
```

## A first grid

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/node_modules/@dzgrid/theme/dzgrid.css">
<style>dz-grid > .dzg { block-size: 420px; }</style>

<dz-grid locale="en-GB" density="compact" label="Moons"></dz-grid>

<script type="module">
  import '@dzgrid/element/define';
  import { EN } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en';

  const grid = document.querySelector('dz-grid');
  grid.columns = [{ id: 'name', header: 'Moon' }, { id: 'found', header: 'Found', type: 'day' }];
  grid.getRowId = (m) => m.id;
  grid.messages = EN;
  grid.rows = [{ id: 'm1', name: 'Quill', found: '2023-05-30' }];
  grid.addEventListener('dzg-row-clicked', (e) => console.log(e.detail.row.key));
</script>
```

The grid is drawn once the element is in the page and has `columns`, `getRowId` and `messages`. The element is
`display: contents`, so size the grid itself: `dz-grid > .dzg { block-size: … }`.

## In TypeScript

The element class is generic over the row type; ask `querySelector` for it.

```ts
import '@dzgrid/element/define';
import type { DzGridElement } from '@dzgrid/element';
import type { GridEvent } from '@dzgrid/core';
import { filters } from '@dzgrid/dom/filters-base';
import { EN } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en';
import { EN_FILTERS } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en-filters';

type Moon = { id: string; name: string; radius: number };

const grid = document.querySelector<DzGridElement<Moon>>('dz-grid')!;
grid.columns = [{ id: 'name', header: 'Moon' }, { id: 'radius', header: 'Radius (km)', type: 'number' }];
grid.getRowId = (m) => m.id;
grid.messages = { ...EN, text: { ...EN.text, ...EN_FILTERS.text } };
grid.features = [filters()];
grid.settings = { selection: { mode: 'single' } };
grid.rows = [{ id: 'm1', name: 'Quill', radius: 812 }];

grid.addEventListener('dzg-sort-changed', (e) => {
  const event = (e as CustomEvent<GridEvent<Moon>>).detail;
  console.log(event.type);
});

await grid.ready;   // resolved when first drawn
grid.grid?.kernel.dispatch({ type: 'quick.set', text: 'quill' }, 'api');
```

## Properties

| Property | What it is |
|---|---|
| `rows`, `source`, `columns`, `getRowId`, `messages`, `features`, `parts` | As `createGrid`'s settings. Live (by identity), except `getRowId` and `features`, read when the grid is made. |
| `settings` | Every other setting (`selection`, `context`, `rowClass`, `pagination`…), compared key by key. |
| `env` | The `GridEnv`, read when the grid is made. |
| `grid` | The `GridInstance` (`kernel`, `api`, `update`) while drawn; `null` otherwise. |
| `ready` | A promise: resolved when first drawn, rejected when the settings are refused. |
| `problems` | The last 100 problems told. |
| `update(patch)` | Same as `grid.update(patch)`. |

Parts are functions made with `definePart` from `@dzgrid/dom`; `<template>` children are not read.

## Attributes

Live, and they win over `settings`; removing one puts the setting back to its default. A value the element cannot
read is left out and reported (`invalid-setting`, path `attribute:<name>`).

`locale`, `time-zone`, `numerals` (`latn` | `locale`), `direction` (`auto` | `ltr` | `rtl`; without it the grid follows
the element's `dir`), `density` (`compact` | `comfortable` | `spacious`), `row-height`, `label`, `overlay` (`loading` |
`error`), `busy`, `motion`, `multi-sort` (read when the grid is made). Booleans: present or `"true"` is on, `"false"` off.

## Events

Every grid event is dispatched on the element as `dzg-` plus its type in kebab case, with the event itself as
`detail`: `dzg-cell-clicked`, `dzg-row-clicked`, `dzg-selection-changed`, `dzg-sort-changed`, `dzg-filter-changed`,
`dzg-row-move`, `dzg-state-changed`, `dzg-problems`… They bubble and are composed. `dzg-ready` follows each making
of the grid. The events of the grid's first drawing come a microtask later, so a listener added right after the last
property still hears them.

## In a framework

React 19 and Vue pass properties to custom elements: bind `columns`, `rows`, `getRowId` and `messages` as
properties, listen to `dzg-*` events. Keep `features` and `getRowId` stable (outside the render function, or memoised):
they are read once.

---

<!-- docs/guide/columns.md -->

# Columns

A column is a plain object (`ColumnDef<T>` from `@dzgrid/core`). Only the keys below exist; an unknown key is
reported as a problem, never guessed. Angular's `DzgColumnDef<T>` is the same object, and also takes component
classes in `ui`.

## Value and type

```ts
import type { ColumnOrGroup } from '@dzgrid/core';
import { textCodec } from '@dzgrid/core';

type Parcel = {
  id: number;
  code: string;
  sender: { name: string; town: string };
  status: string;
  weight: number;
  sentOn: string;
  arrivedAt: number | null;
  insured: boolean;
};

const shout = { ...textCodec, format: (v: string) => v.toUpperCase() };

export const columns: ColumnOrGroup<Parcel>[] = [
  { id: 'code', header: 'Code', width: 110, pinned: 'start', codec: shout },
  { id: 'sender', header: 'Sender', field: 'sender.name', flex: 2, minWidth: 160 },
  { id: 'status', header: 'Status', type: 'enum', enumOptions: [{ value: 'open', label: 'Open' }, { value: 'done', label: 'Delivered' }] },
  { id: 'weight', header: 'Weight', type: 'number', align: 'end', numberFormat: { maximumFractionDigits: 2 } },
  { id: 'sentOn', header: 'Sent on', type: 'day' },
  { id: 'arrivedAt', header: 'Arrived', type: 'instant', instantFormat: { date: true, time: true } },
  { id: 'insured', header: 'Insured', type: 'boolean' },
  { id: 'heavy', header: 'Heavy', type: 'boolean', value: (p) => p.weight > 20, sortable: false, filter: false },
];
```

- `id` is required, unique and stable. The value is read from `field` (a dotted path, own properties only; by default
  the `id`), or computed by `value(row)`.
- `type`: `text` (default), `number`, `day`, `instant`, `boolean`, `enum`, `custom`.
- A `day` is a `'YYYY-MM-DD'` string. An `instant` is epoch milliseconds or ISO text **with** an offset (`Z`,
  `+02:00`). Text with no offset is ambiguous: the cell is blank and an `ambiguous-instant` problem is reported,
  unless the column says which zone to read it in with `assumeZone: 'Europe/Paris'`. A JavaScript `Date` is not
  read: pass `date.getTime()`.
- What a cell shows comes from the type and `numberFormat`, `instantFormat`, `enumOptions`, or a whole `codec` (read,
  format, sort). Instants are shown in the grid's `timeZone`.

## Size and place

`width`, `minWidth`, `maxWidth` (px), `flex` (a share of the room left), `resizable`, `movable`, `pinned: 'start' |
'end'`, `hidden`, `align: 'start' | 'center' | 'end'`, `wrap` (several lines; rows grow with the `autoHeight()`
feature from `@dzgrid/dom/auto-height`). Sides are logical: `start` is the left in English and the right in Arabic.

## Column groups

A group has `children` and an optional `header`; `collapsible` groups fold to the columns marked
`groupShow: 'closed'`. Group header rows need the `spans()` feature.

```ts
import { createGrid } from '@dzgrid/dom';
import type { ColumnOrGroup } from '@dzgrid/core';
import { spans } from '@dzgrid/dom/spans';
import { EN } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en';

type Station = { id: string; name: string; tempMin: number; tempMax: number; rain: number };

const columns: ColumnOrGroup<Station>[] = [
  { id: 'name', header: 'Station' },
  { id: 'weather', header: 'Weather', collapsible: true, children: [
    { id: 'tempMin', header: 'Min °C', type: 'number' },
    { id: 'tempMax', header: 'Max °C', type: 'number', groupShow: 'closed' },
    { id: 'rain', header: 'Rain (mm)', type: 'number' },
  ] },
];

createGrid<Station>(document.getElementById('stations')!, {
  rows: [{ id: 's1', name: 'Cape Lumen', tempMin: 4, tempMax: 17, rain: 2.5 }],
  columns,
  getRowId: (s) => s.id,
  messages: EN,
  features: [spans()],
});
```

`spans()` also merges cells: `merge: true` on a column joins equal neighbours, `rowSpan(ctx)` and `colSpan(ctx)`
decide from the data, and the `fullWidth` setting draws a row across every column.

## Classes, tooltips, custom cells

- `ui.cellClass(c)` returns a class for one cell; `ui.headerClass` a class for the header; the grid setting
  `rowClass(c)` a class for a row.
- `tooltip(value, row, context)` returns the text shown on hover and focus; `headerTooltip` the header's.
- `ui.cell`, `ui.header`, `ui.tooltip` name a part (custom drawing, see below).

```ts
import { createGrid, definePart } from '@dzgrid/dom';
import { EN } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en';
import '@dzgrid/theme/dzgrid.css';

type Bee = { id: string; hive: string; honey: number };

const jar = definePart('cell', {
  mount(host, c) {
    const span = host.ownerDocument.createElement('span');
    host.append(span);
    const draw = (n: typeof c) => { span.textContent = n.value == null ? '' : `${n.text} kg`; };
    draw(c);
    return { update: draw, destroy: () => span.remove() };
  },
});

createGrid<Bee>(document.getElementById('hives')!, {
  rows: [{ id: 'h1', hive: 'Clover hill', honey: 12.5 }],
  columns: [
    { id: 'hive', header: 'Hive', tooltip: (v) => (v ? `Hive ${v}` : null) },
    { id: 'honey', header: 'Honey', type: 'number', ui: { cell: 'jar', cellClass: (c) => (Number(c.value) > 10 ? 'is-full' : null) } },
  ],
  getRowId: (b) => b.id,
  messages: EN,
  parts: { jar },
  rowClass: (c) => (c.row.honey === 0 ? 'is-empty' : null),
});
```

The grid never writes HTML strings: a part builds DOM in the host it is given, and the grid keeps the cell's role,
focus and keyboard. Header, tooltip and overlay parts need the `slots()` feature from `@dzgrid/dom/slots`. Ready-made
cells (`badge`, `cellBoolean`) are in `@dzgrid/dom/parts`.

## Moving, resizing, hiding

- `columns()` from `@dzgrid/dom/columns`: drag a header to move it, drag its edge to resize, double click the edge to
  fit the content; the keyboard does the same (texts `-columns`, CSS `columns.css`).
- `columnMenu()` from `@dzgrid/dom/column-menu`: the menu on each header (sort, pin, size, hide, group…; texts
  `-column-menu`, CSS `menu.css`). Give it the other features it can drive in `use`.
- `columnsChooser()` from `@dzgrid/dom/columns-panel`: a panel to show, hide and order columns (see
  [Dock and panels](https://github.com/plinthworks/dzgrid/blob/main/docs/guide/dock-panels.md)).

```ts
import { createGrid, type GridMessages } from '@dzgrid/dom';
import { columns } from '@dzgrid/dom/columns';
import { columnMenu } from '@dzgrid/dom/column-menu';
import { columnsChooser } from '@dzgrid/dom/columns-panel';
import { EN } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en';
import { EN_COLUMNS } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en-columns';
import { EN_COLUMN_MENU } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en-column-menu';
import '@dzgrid/theme/dzgrid.css';
import '@dzgrid/theme/columns.css';
import '@dzgrid/theme/menu.css';
import '@dzgrid/theme/columns-panel.css';

type Shell = { id: string; name: string; beach: string; size: number };

const moves = columns();
const chooser = columnsChooser();
const messages: GridMessages = { ...EN, text: { ...EN.text, ...EN_COLUMNS.text, ...EN_COLUMN_MENU.text } };

const grid = createGrid<Shell>(document.getElementById('shells')!, {
  rows: [{ id: 'x1', name: 'Spiral cone', beach: 'Amber bay', size: 4.2 }],
  columns: [{ id: 'name', header: 'Shell' }, { id: 'beach', header: 'Beach' }, { id: 'size', header: 'Size (cm)', type: 'number' }],
  getRowId: (s) => s.id,
  messages,
  features: [moves, chooser, columnMenu({ use: { columns: moves, chooser } })],
});

moves.api(grid)?.autoSizeAll();
grid.kernel.dispatch({ type: 'column.state', patch: [{ id: 'beach', hidden: true }] }, 'api');
```

Every feature that has an api gives it through `feature.api(grid)` (in Angular, `ctrl.use(feature)`); it is `null`
until the grid exists.

---

<!-- docs/guide/sort-filter-search.md -->

# Sort, filter and search

## Sorting

Sorting needs no feature: a click on a header sorts, a second click reverses, Shift+click adds the column to the
sort; from the keyboard, Enter and Shift+Enter on a header do the same. `sortable: false` on a column turns it off; the `multiSort: false` setting keeps one key.
Text sorts follow the grid's `locale` (Arabic letters, accents, digits). Empty cells are last in both directions
(`nulls: 'first'` in a sort item puts them first).

There is no sort key on a column. Sort from code with a command, or set the first sort with the
[state](https://github.com/plinthworks/dzgrid/blob/main/docs/guide/state.md) feature (`gridState({ initial })`, which sends a single request to a server).

```ts
import { createGrid } from '@dzgrid/dom';
import { EN } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en';

type River = { id: string; name: string; length: number };

const grid = createGrid<River>(document.getElementById('rivers')!, {
  rows: [{ id: 'r1', name: 'Silverrun', length: 412 }, { id: 'r2', name: 'Oxbow', length: 96 }],
  columns: [{ id: 'name', header: 'River' }, { id: 'length', header: 'Length (km)', type: 'number' }],
  getRowId: (r) => r.id,
  messages: EN,
});

grid.kernel.dispatch({ type: 'sort.set', sort: [{ column: 'length', dir: 'desc' }] }, 'api');
grid.kernel.dispatch({ type: 'sort.toggle', column: 'name', multi: true }, 'api');
console.log(grid.kernel.query.sort);
```

## Column filters

`filters()` adds a filter button to each header and a filter popup: text, number, day, instant, yes/no, and a value
list (`kind: 'set'`). Import it from `@dzgrid/dom/filters` (date filters with a calendar, needs `@tzslot/*`) or
`@dzgrid/dom/filters-base` (no calendar). Texts: `-filters`.

```ts
import { createGrid, type GridMessages } from '@dzgrid/dom';
import type { ColumnOrGroup } from '@dzgrid/core';
import { filters } from '@dzgrid/dom/filters-base';
import { EN } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en';
import { EN_FILTERS } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en-filters';

type Recipe = { id: string; name: string; cuisine: string; minutes: number; vegan: boolean };

const columns: ColumnOrGroup<Recipe>[] = [
  { id: 'name', header: 'Recipe', filter: { kind: 'text', debounceMs: 200 } },
  { id: 'cuisine', header: 'Cuisine', filter: { kind: 'set' } },
  { id: 'minutes', header: 'Minutes', type: 'number', filter: { maxConditions: 2 } },
  { id: 'vegan', header: 'Vegan', type: 'boolean' },
];
const messages: GridMessages = { ...EN, text: { ...EN.text, ...EN_FILTERS.text } };

const grid = createGrid<Recipe>(document.getElementById('recipes')!, {
  rows: [{ id: 'c1', name: 'Moon soup', cuisine: 'Lunar', minutes: 25, vegan: true }],
  columns,
  getRowId: (r) => r.id,
  messages,
  features: [filters({ floating: true, apply: 'live' })],
});

grid.kernel.dispatch({ type: 'filter.column', column: 'minutes', filter: { type: 'number', op: 'lte', value: 30 } }, 'api');
grid.kernel.dispatch({ type: 'filter.column', column: 'cuisine', filter: { type: 'set', include: ['Lunar'] } }, 'api');
grid.kernel.dispatch({ type: 'filter.set', filter: {} }, 'api');   // clears every filter
```

- `floating: true` adds a row of small filter fields under the headers; `apply: 'button'` waits for the Apply
  button instead of filtering as you type.
- `filter: false` on a column removes its filter; `filter.ops` limits the operators offered.
- A filter on a `day` or `instant` column is resolved in the grid's `timeZone`, half-open, to the millisecond —
  also when it is sent to a server.
- The filter shapes (`ColumnFilter`): `text`, `number`, `day`, `instant`, `boolean`, `set`, `combined` (`and` / `or`
  of conditions), `custom` (your own kind, registered with the `filterKinds` setting).

## The filters panel

`filtersPanel()` from `@dzgrid/dom/filters-panel` lists every column's filter in a side panel (texts
`-filters-panel`, CSS `filters-panel.css`). Inside a [dock](https://github.com/plinthworks/dzgrid/blob/main/docs/guide/dock-panels.md) it becomes one of the dock's panels.

## Quick search

`quickSearch()` from `@dzgrid/dom/search` filters on every visible column at once, from an input you own; matches are
highlighted (CSS `search.css`).

```ts
import { createGrid } from '@dzgrid/dom';
import { quickSearch } from '@dzgrid/dom/search';
import { EN } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en';
import '@dzgrid/theme/search.css';

type Cloud = { id: string; name: string; height: number };

const search = quickSearch({ highlight: true });
createGrid<Cloud>(document.getElementById('clouds')!, {
  rows: [{ id: 'n1', name: 'Cirrus feather', height: 9000 }],
  columns: [{ id: 'name', header: 'Cloud' }, { id: 'height', header: 'Height (m)', type: 'number' }],
  getRowId: (c) => c.id,
  messages: EN,
  features: [search],
});
search.bind(document.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>('#cloud-search')!, { debounceMs: 150 });
```

In Angular, `<input [dzgSearch]="search">` (directive `DzgSearch`) binds the same feature; the `[(quick)]` model holds
the text. Searching follows the language: Arabic letters with or without hamza and short vowels, Arabic-Indic digits.

## Find (Ctrl+F)

`find()` from `@dzgrid/dom/find` replaces the browser's Ctrl+F inside the grid: it marks a text in the cells of every row the filters keep
(rows inside closed tree nodes too) and walks the focus from hit to hit with Enter and Shift+Enter, without hiding any
row (texts `-find`, CSS `find.css`).

---

<!-- docs/guide/selection-ranges.md -->

# Selection and ranges

Two different things: **rows** are selected (a set of rows, for an action on them), **cells** are taken in a
**block** (a rectangle, for copy, paste and fill).

## Selecting rows

The `selection` setting turns it on; no feature is needed.

```ts
import { createGrid } from '@dzgrid/dom';
import { idOfDataKey, type SelectionState } from '@dzgrid/core';
import { EN } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en';

type Seed = { id: string; plant: string; packets: number };

const grid = createGrid<Seed>(document.getElementById('seeds')!, {
  rows: [{ id: 's1', plant: 'Moon squash', packets: 12 }, { id: 's2', plant: 'Glass bean', packets: 0 }],
  columns: [{ id: 'plant', header: 'Plant' }, { id: 'packets', header: 'Packets', type: 'number' }],
  getRowId: (s) => s.id,
  messages: EN,
  selection: { mode: 'multi', checkbox: true, keepOnFilter: true },
  onEvent: (e) => {
    if (e.type === 'selectionChanged') console.log(describe(e.selection), e.count);
  },
});

function describe(s: SelectionState): string {
  const ids = [...s.keys].map(idOfDataKey);
  return s.mode === 'include' ? `only ${ids.join(', ')}` : `every row but ${ids.join(', ')}`;
}

grid.kernel.dispatch({ type: 'selection.all' }, 'api');
```

- `mode`: `none`, `single` or `multi`. `checkbox: true` adds a tick column with a header box; `click: false` leaves
  clicks to focus only (select with Space or the box).
- Click selects one row, Ctrl/Cmd+click toggles, Shift+click selects a run in screen order; Space toggles the focused
  row, Ctrl+A selects all. The selection survives sorting and filtering.
- The selection holds **row keys**, not your ids. `idOfDataKey(key)` gives the id back; in Angular,
  `selectedIds(controller)` gives the ids of the whole selection with the query.
- `mode: 'exclude'` means « every row the query matches, but these keys »: after « select all » on paged or server
  rows, the grid cannot list them, your server can by replaying the query.
- `canSelect(row, selection, context)` returns `false`, or a reason code, to refuse a row; it needs the `rules()`
  feature from `@dzgrid/dom/rules` (texts `-rules`), which says why to the user.

## Blocks of cells and the clipboard

`range()` from `@dzgrid/dom/range` adds blocks: Shift+arrows, a drag, Ctrl+A. Ctrl+C copies the block as tab-separated
text that spreadsheets read (numbers in the locale's form, formula starts guarded), Ctrl+X cuts, Ctrl+V pastes into
editable cells, Delete empties them. Pasting and cutting need [editing](https://github.com/plinthworks/dzgrid/blob/main/docs/guide/editing.md). Texts `-range`, CSS `range.css`.

`fill(blocks)` from `@dzgrid/dom/fill` adds the fill handle at the block's corner: drag it to copy the block on, or to
continue a series (1, 2, 3…; days by days); Ctrl+D and Ctrl+R fill down and right from the keyboard. Texts `-fill`, CSS
`fill.css`. A fill or a paste is one save request and one undo.

```ts
import { createGrid, type GridMessages } from '@dzgrid/dom';
import { edit } from '@dzgrid/dom/edit';
import { editors } from '@dzgrid/dom/editors-base';
import { range } from '@dzgrid/dom/range';
import { fill } from '@dzgrid/dom/fill';
import { EN } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en';
import { EN_EDIT } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en-edit';
import { EN_EDITORS } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en-editors';
import { EN_RANGE } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en-range';
import { EN_FILL } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en-fill';
import '@dzgrid/theme/edit.css';
import '@dzgrid/theme/range.css';
import '@dzgrid/theme/fill.css';

type Shelf = { id: string; aisle: string; jars: number };

const blocks = range();
const handle = fill(blocks);
const messages: GridMessages = {
  ...EN,
  text: { ...EN.text, ...EN_EDIT.text, ...EN_EDITORS.text, ...EN_RANGE.text, ...EN_FILL.text },
};

const grid = createGrid<Shelf>(document.getElementById('pantry')!, {
  rows: [{ id: 'a1', aisle: 'Jam', jars: 14 }, { id: 'a2', aisle: 'Honey', jars: 9 }],
  columns: [
    { id: 'aisle', header: 'Aisle' },
    { id: 'jars', header: 'Jars', type: 'number', editable: true },
  ],
  getRowId: (s) => s.id,
  messages,
  features: [edit<Shelf>(), editors(), blocks, handle],
  onEvent: (e) => {
    if (e.type === 'rangeCopied') console.log(`${e.cells} cells copied`);
  },
});

const copied = blocks.api(grid)?.copy({ headers: true });   // the block as text, as Ctrl+C would
console.log(copied);
```

The right-click menu (`contextMenu({ use: { range: blocks, fill: handle } })` from `@dzgrid/dom/context-menu`) offers
the same actions to the mouse.

---

<!-- docs/guide/editing.md -->

# Editing

Two features: `edit()` from `@dzgrid/dom/edit` holds the edits (save, undo, refusals; texts `-edit`, CSS `edit.css`),
`editors()` draws the fields (texts `-editors`). Take `editors` from `@dzgrid/dom/editors` (a date calendar from
`@tzslot/*`, loaded on first use) or from `@dzgrid/dom/editors-base` (no calendar).

F2, Enter, a double click or typing a character opens the field; Enter keeps the value and moves down (`enterMoves`),
Tab moves to the next editable cell, Escape gives the old value back.

```ts
import { createGrid } from '@dzgrid/dom';
import type { ColumnOrGroup } from '@dzgrid/core';
import type { SaveRequest } from '@dzgrid/core/edit';
import { edit } from '@dzgrid/dom/edit';
import { editors } from '@dzgrid/dom/editors-base';
import { EN } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en';
import { EN_EDIT } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en-edit';
import { EN_EDITORS } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en-editors';
import '@dzgrid/theme/dzgrid.css';
import '@dzgrid/theme/edit.css';

type Gnome = { id: string; name: string; hat: string; height: number; painted: string; locked: boolean };

const columns: ColumnOrGroup<Gnome>[] = [
  { id: 'name', header: 'Name', editable: (g) => !g.locked, edit: { required: true, maxLength: 40 } },
  { id: 'hat', header: 'Hat', type: 'enum', editable: true,
    edit: { options: [{ value: 'red', label: 'Red' }, { value: 'green', label: 'Green' }] } },
  { id: 'height', header: 'Height (cm)', type: 'number', editable: true, edit: { min: 5, max: 120 },
    validate: (v) => (typeof v === 'number' && v % 1 !== 0 ? 'whole' : null) },
  { id: 'painted', header: 'Painted on', type: 'day', editable: true },
];

async function save(req: SaveRequest<Gnome>, signal: AbortSignal): Promise<void> {
  const body = req.changes.map((c) => ({ id: c.row.id, column: c.column, value: c.value }));
  const answer = await fetch('/api/gnomes', { method: 'PATCH', body: JSON.stringify(body), signal });
  if (!answer.ok) throw Object.assign(new Error('refused'), { reason: await answer.text() });
}

// Not typed `GridMessages`: an app's own `validation.<code>` keys are extra keys.
const messages = {
  ...EN,
  text: { ...EN.text, ...EN_EDIT.text, ...EN_EDITORS.text, 'validation.whole': 'a whole number' },
};

const grid = createGrid<Gnome>(document.getElementById('gnomes')!, {
  rows: [{ id: 'g1', name: 'Barnaby', hat: 'red', height: 31, painted: '2025-04-02', locked: false }],
  columns,
  getRowId: (g) => g.id,
  messages,
  features: [edit<Gnome>({ save: (req, signal) => save(req, signal as AbortSignal) }), editors({ enterMoves: 'down' })],
  onEvent: (e) => {
    if (e.type === 'cellEdited') console.log(e.column, e.previous, '→', e.value, e.origin);
    if (e.type === 'saveFailed') console.warn('not saved', e.column, e.reason);
  },
});
```

## Checks

- `editable`: `true`, or a function `(row, context, info)`; a cell that cannot be edited answers « read-only ».
- `edit`: `required`, `min`, `max`, `pattern`, `maxLength`, `options` (a list, or a function of the row), and
  `editor` (the name of your own editor part).
- `validate(value, row, context)` returns a code, or `null` when the value is fine. Give the code's sentence in
  `messages` as `validation.<code>`; without it, a generic « invalid » is said.
- A refused value stays in the open field, blinks, and is said to screen readers with the column's name and the reason.

## Saving

`save(request, signal)` receives one request per gesture (`request.changes`: `key`, `column`, `value`, `previous`,
`row`; `request.origin` says whether it was an edit, a paste, a fill, an undo…). Resolve: saved. Reject or throw:
refused — the cells go back, and an error with a string `reason` shows that reason. Without `save`, edits are kept in
the grid only (you hear `cellEdited` and may apply it to your rows). While a save runs, the cell shows a moving
border and says « saving » to screen readers. Saves of one cell go in order: a newer gesture waits for the older one.
The grid never writes into your rows: a kept value is shown over the row until your rows (a new array, a transaction,
a server answer) carry it. Hand `signal` on to `fetch`.

## Undo and redo

Ctrl+Z undoes, Ctrl+Y or Ctrl+Shift+Z redoes (Cmd on a Mac), over the last 100 gestures, each going through `save` again. From code:

```ts
import { createGrid } from '@dzgrid/dom';
import { edit } from '@dzgrid/dom/edit';
import { editors } from '@dzgrid/dom/editors-base';
import { EN } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en';
import { EN_EDIT } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en-edit';
import { EN_EDITORS } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en-editors';

type Note = { id: string; text: string };

const editing = edit<Note>();
const grid = createGrid<Note>(document.getElementById('notes')!, {
  rows: [{ id: 'n1', text: 'Feed the dragon' }],
  columns: [{ id: 'text', header: 'Note', editable: true }],
  getRowId: (n) => n.id,
  messages: { ...EN, text: { ...EN.text, ...EN_EDIT.text, ...EN_EDITORS.text } },
  features: [editing, editors()],
  onEvent: (e) => {
    if (e.type === 'undoChanged') console.log('can undo:', e.canUndo, 'can redo:', e.canRedo);
  },
});

document.getElementById('undo')!.addEventListener('click', () => editing.api(grid)?.undo());
```

In Angular: `[save]="save"` on `<dz-grid>`, `(cellEdited)`, `(saveFailed)`, `(undoChanged)`, and
`ctrl.edit()?.undo()`.

## Your own editor

An `editor` part draws the field; its context's `keep(input)` keeps a value (through the same checks and save),
`cancel()` closes without one, `refuse(code)` refuses with a reason. Register it under
a name and point the column's `edit.editor` at it (or name it `editor.<type>` to replace an editor for a whole type).
A ready list editor with search is `listEditor()` from `@dzgrid/dom/editors-list`.

---

<!-- docs/guide/tree.md -->

# Tree

`tree()` from `@dzgrid/dom/tree` shows rows as a tree (a WAI-ARIA treegrid): the tree column is indented one step per
level, a parent has a chevron, → opens it, ← closes it or goes to the parent (mirrored in right to left), `*` opens
its siblings. Texts `-tree`. Tree rows are ordinary
data rows with ordinary keys: selection, editing and export work on them as on flat rows.

Give the hierarchy one of three ways:

| Option | Your rows | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `parentId(row)` | flat, each with its parent's id (`null` at the top) | folders in a table |
| `children(row)` | nested, each holding its children | a JSON document |
| `path(row)` | flat, each with its path of names | `['Garden', 'Tools', 'Rake']` |

```ts
import { createGrid, type GridMessages } from '@dzgrid/dom';
import { tree } from '@dzgrid/dom/tree';
import { EN } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en';
import { EN_TREE } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en-tree';

type Room = { id: string; parent: string | null; name: string; area: number };

const rows: Room[] = [
  { id: 'h', parent: null, name: 'Lighthouse', area: 120 },
  { id: 'h1', parent: 'h', name: 'Lamp room', area: 14 },
  { id: 'h2', parent: 'h', name: 'Keeper’s kitchen', area: 22 },
  { id: 'h21', parent: 'h2', name: 'Pantry', area: 4 },
];
const messages: GridMessages = { ...EN, text: { ...EN.text, ...EN_TREE.text } };

const rooms = tree<Room>({ parentId: (r) => r.parent, initial: 1, column: 'name', filter: 'ancestors' });
const grid = createGrid<Room>(document.getElementById('rooms')!, {
  rows,
  columns: [{ id: 'name', header: 'Room', flex: 1 }, { id: 'area', header: 'Area (m²)', type: 'number' }],
  getRowId: (r) => r.id,
  messages,
  features: [rooms],
});

grid.kernel.dispatch({ type: 'rows.expandAll', expanded: true }, 'api');
```

- `initial`: `'none'` (all closed), `'all'`, or a depth (open down to that level).
- `filter`: `'ancestors'` keeps the parents of a matching row (so it can be reached), `'subtree'` also keeps the
  children of a matching parent.
- A sort orders each parent's children among themselves; parents stay above their children. What is open stays open
  after a sort, a filter or new rows.
- `sticky: n` keeps the open parents of the rows in view pinned under the header, up to `n` levels.
- `column` is the tree column (the first visible column by default); `indent` its step in pixels.
- `rows.expand` and `rows.expandAll` commands open and close from code; `rowExpanded` events tell you. In Angular,
  `[(expanded)]` holds the open keys.

## Children loaded on demand

`lazyChildren({ has, load })` from `@dzgrid/dom/tree-lazy` loads a parent's children when it is first opened: `has(row)`
says whether a row may have children (it gets a chevron), `load(row, { signal })` returns them. While they load, a
loading row stands under the parent; a failure there offers a retry.

```ts
import { createGrid } from '@dzgrid/dom';
import { tree } from '@dzgrid/dom/tree';
import { lazyChildren } from '@dzgrid/dom/tree-lazy';
import { EN } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en';
import { EN_TREE } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en-tree';

type Folder = { id: string; parent: string | null; name: string; folders: number };

createGrid<Folder>(document.getElementById('folders')!, {
  rows: [{ id: 'root', parent: null, name: 'Archive of maps', folders: 3 }],
  columns: [{ id: 'name', header: 'Folder' }],
  getRowId: (f) => f.id,
  messages: { ...EN, text: { ...EN.text, ...EN_TREE.text } },
  features: [tree<Folder>({
    parentId: (f) => f.parent,
    lazy: lazyChildren<Folder>({
      has: (f) => f.folders > 0,
      load: async (f, { signal }) => (await fetch(`/api/folders/${f.id}`, { signal: signal as AbortSignal })).json(),
    }),
  })],
});
```

## Master and detail

`detail({ part, height })` from `@dzgrid/dom/detail` opens a panel under a row instead of child rows (texts `-detail`).
The panel is a `detail` part; `nestedGrid({ settings })` makes that part a whole grid of its own. Nesting stops past
three levels.

```ts
import { createGrid } from '@dzgrid/dom';
import { detail, nestedGrid } from '@dzgrid/dom/detail';
import { EN } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en';
import { EN_DETAIL } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en-detail';

type Trip = { id: string; date: string; km: number };
type Bicycle = { id: string; name: string; trips: Trip[] };

const messages = { ...EN, text: { ...EN.text, ...EN_DETAIL.text } };
const trips = nestedGrid<Trip>({
  settings: (c) => ({
    rows: (c.row as Bicycle).trips,
    columns: [{ id: 'date', header: 'Date', type: 'day' }, { id: 'km', header: 'km', type: 'number' }],
    getRowId: (t) => t.id,
    messages,
  }),
});

createGrid<Bicycle>(document.getElementById('bicycles')!, {
  rows: [{ id: 'b1', name: 'Blue heron', trips: [{ id: 't1', date: '2026-06-01', km: 42 }] }],
  columns: [{ id: 'name', header: 'Bicycle' }],
  getRowId: (b) => b.id,
  messages,
  features: [detail<Bicycle>({ part: trips, height: 200 })],
});
```

In Angular the panel is a component given with `componentPart('detail', Component)`, and a `<dz-grid [dzgNested]>` inside
it makes the nested grid.

---

<!-- docs/guide/grouping.md -->

# Grouping

`grouping({ by })` from `@dzgrid/dom/grouping` gathers rows under group rows, one level per column in `by`, with
totals (texts `-group`, CSS `grouping.css`). The group rows are drawn in a group column; → and ← open and close them,
Enter toggles.

```ts
import { createGrid, type GridMessages } from '@dzgrid/dom';
import type { ColumnOrGroup } from '@dzgrid/core';
import { grouping } from '@dzgrid/dom/grouping';
import { groupZone } from '@dzgrid/dom/group-zone';
import { columns } from '@dzgrid/dom/columns';
import { columnMenu } from '@dzgrid/dom/column-menu';
import { EN } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en';
import { EN_GROUP } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en-group';
import { EN_COLUMNS } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en-columns';
import { EN_COLUMN_MENU } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en-column-menu';
import '@dzgrid/theme/dzgrid.css';
import '@dzgrid/theme/grouping.css';
import '@dzgrid/theme/columns.css';
import '@dzgrid/theme/menu.css';

type Sale = { id: string; island: string; stall: string; fruit: string; crates: number; price: number };

const cols: ColumnOrGroup<Sale>[] = [
  { id: 'island', header: 'Island' },
  { id: 'stall', header: 'Stall' },
  { id: 'fruit', header: 'Fruit', aggFunc: 'count' },
  { id: 'crates', header: 'Crates', type: 'number', aggFunc: 'sum' },
  { id: 'price', header: 'Price (avg.)', type: 'number', aggFunc: 'avg', numberFormat: { maximumFractionDigits: 2 } },
];
const messages: GridMessages = { ...EN, text: { ...EN.text, ...EN_GROUP.text, ...EN_COLUMNS.text, ...EN_COLUMN_MENU.text } };

const groups = grouping({ by: ['island', 'stall'], expanded: 1, footers: 'grand', grandTotal: 'bottom' });
const moves = columns();
const grid = createGrid<Sale>(document.getElementById('market')!, {
  rows: [
    { id: 's1', island: 'Maru', stall: 'North pier', fruit: 'Starfruit', crates: 4, price: 3.2 },
    { id: 's2', island: 'Maru', stall: 'Old well', fruit: 'Guava', crates: 7, price: 2.1 },
    { id: 's3', island: 'Teva', stall: 'Reef gate', fruit: 'Mango', crates: 2, price: 4.5 },
  ],
  columns: cols,
  getRowId: (s) => s.id,
  messages,
  features: [moves, groups, groupZone({ use: { grouping: groups, columns: moves } }), columnMenu({ use: { grouping: groups, columns: moves } })],
});

const api = groups.api(grid);
api?.setBy(['fruit']);
api?.expandAll();
console.log(api?.totals());
```

- `by`: the columns to group by, outermost first. Change it with `api.setBy(ids)`, or let the user do it: the drop
  band `groupZone()` from `@dzgrid/dom/group-zone` (drag a header into it), or « Group by this column » in the column
  menu. A column with `groupable: false` cannot be grouped by.
- Totals: a column's `aggFunc` — `sum`, `avg`, `min`, `max`, `count`, `first`, `last`, or your own function — or
  `aggFuncs: { column: fn }` in the options. A group row shows its totals in those columns.
- `expanded`: `'none'`, `'all'` or a depth. `footers`: `'group'` adds a total row under each group, `'grand'` a grand
  total, `'both'`. `grandTotal`: `'top'` or `'bottom'`.
- `api.expandAll(depth?)`, `api.collapseAll()`; the `rows.expandAll` command does the same.
- Sorting a grouped column sorts the groups; other sorts sort the rows inside each group.
- In Angular, `[(groupBy)]` holds the grouped columns and `ctrl.grouping()` gives the api.

## Groups on a server

When the rows live on a server, `serverSideRows({ by })` from `@dzgrid/core/server-side` asks the server for one level
at a time: see [Server data](https://github.com/plinthworks/dzgrid/blob/main/docs/guide/server-data.md).

---

<!-- docs/guide/pivot.md -->

# Pivot

A pivot table adds an axis across [grouping](https://github.com/plinthworks/dzgrid/blob/main/docs/guide/grouping.md): the rows are the groups, each value of the pivot columns
becomes a column, and each cell totals the value columns where a group and a column meet. `pivot()` from
`@dzgrid/dom/pivot` is given to `grouping({ pivot })`, which draws it (texts `-pivot`, CSS `pivot.css`). The value
columns' headers need `spans()`.

```ts
import { createGrid, type GridMessages } from '@dzgrid/dom';
import type { ColumnOrGroup } from '@dzgrid/core';
import { grouping } from '@dzgrid/dom/grouping';
import { pivot } from '@dzgrid/dom/pivot';
import { pivotBar } from '@dzgrid/dom/pivot-bar';
import { spans } from '@dzgrid/dom/spans';
import { groups } from '@dzgrid/dom/groups';
import { columns } from '@dzgrid/dom/columns';
import { EN } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en';
import { EN_GROUP } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en-group';
import { EN_PIVOT } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en-pivot';
import { EN_PIVOT_BAR } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en-pivot-bar';
import { EN_COLUMNS } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en-columns';
import '@dzgrid/theme/dzgrid.css';
import '@dzgrid/theme/grouping.css';
import '@dzgrid/theme/pivot.css';
import '@dzgrid/theme/columns.css';

type Ticket = { id: string; cinema: string; month: string; film: string; seats: number; takings: number };

const cols: ColumnOrGroup<Ticket>[] = [
  { id: 'cinema', header: 'Cinema' },
  { id: 'month', header: 'Month' },
  { id: 'film', header: 'Film' },
  { id: 'seats', header: 'Seats', type: 'number' },
  { id: 'takings', header: 'Takings', type: 'number', numberFormat: { style: 'currency', currency: 'EUR' } },
];
const messages: GridMessages = {
  ...EN,
  text: { ...EN.text, ...EN_GROUP.text, ...EN_PIVOT.text, ...EN_PIVOT_BAR.text, ...EN_COLUMNS.text },
};

const cross = pivot({ columns: ['month'], values: { seats: 'sum', takings: 'sum' }, subtotals: true });
const rowsBy = grouping({ by: ['cinema'], pivot: cross });
const moves = columns();
const grid = createGrid<Ticket>(document.getElementById('box-office')!, {
  rows: [
    { id: 't1', cinema: 'The Comet', month: '2026-01', film: 'Paper Tides', seats: 120, takings: 960 },
    { id: 't2', cinema: 'The Comet', month: '2026-02', film: 'Paper Tides', seats: 80, takings: 640 },
    { id: 't3', cinema: 'Orchard Hall', month: '2026-01', film: 'Nine Lanterns', seats: 45, takings: 405 },
  ],
  columns: cols,
  getRowId: (t) => t.id,
  messages,
  features: [spans(), groups(), moves, rowsBy, pivotBar({ use: { grouping: rowsBy, pivot: cross, columns: moves } })],
});

const api = cross.api(grid);
api?.setBy(['month', 'film']);                   // two levels of columns
api?.setValues({ seats: 'avg', takings: 'sum' });
const chart = api?.series({ value: 'takings' });  // { categories, series: [{ id, name, values }] }
console.log(chart?.categories, chart?.series.length);
```

- `columns`: the pivot columns, outermost first; `values`: each value column and how it is totalled (`sum`, `avg`,
  `min`, `max`, `count`, `first`, `last`). `desc` lists the pivot columns whose order is reversed.
- `subtotals: true` adds a total column after each band. `maxColumns` (200 by default) caps how many columns are
  made: past it, none is made, the rows stay grouped with their totals, and the grid says how many there would have
  been (problem `pivot-too-many`). The row side is the grouping: its `by`, totals and opening rules hold.
- `pivotBar()` from `@dzgrid/dom/pivot-bar` draws a bar « Rows │ Columns │ Values » where the user moves columns
  between parts, reverses an order, or changes a value's function (texts `-pivot-bar`).
- Pivot mode is the application's: `toggle: true` (or an element of yours) shows a switch to turn it on and off;
  otherwise `api.setOn(on)`.
- `api.series()` gives the numbers of one value column, ready for a chart library of your own: DzGrid draws no chart.

## Pivot on a server

`serverSideRows(data, { pivot: serverPivot() })`, with `serverPivot` from `@dzgrid/core/server-pivot`, lets the server
compute the crossings; the request's `group` then carries the pivot columns in use and their limit. The features stay
the same (`spans()`, `grouping({ by, pivot })`). See the behaviour sheet [`server-pivot.md`](https://github.com/plinthworks/dzgrid/blob/main/docs/behaviors/server-pivot.md).

---

<!-- docs/guide/server-data.md -->

# Server data and infinite scroll

When the rows live on a server, give the grid a `source` instead of `rows`. Three sources, from `@dzgrid/core`:

| Source | Entry | What the user gets |
|---|---|---|
| `sourceRows(data)` | `@dzgrid/core/server` | pages (with the pager footer), or every row the server's filter keeps |
| `infiniteRows(data)` | `@dzgrid/core/infinite` | one long list, loaded in blocks while scrolling; blocks far away are let go |
| `serverSideRows(data, { by })` | `@dzgrid/core/server-side` | groups computed by the server, each group's rows loaded in blocks |

Each takes the same `DataSource`: a `fetch(request)` that returns (or resolves to) `{ rows, total?, hasNext?,
nextCursor? }`, and optionally `values(request)` for the set filter's value list.

## How it works, in pictures

The idea is simple once seen, and surprising the first time: **the grid builds the request itself and calls your
back end**. You do not keep the filters, the sort or the page in a store, and you do not cache the rows: the grid
owns them. The pictures below follow a made-up observatory's asteroid catalogue.

### Who does what

```text
A grid that only displays                       DzGrid with a source
──────────────────────────                      ────────────────────
user filters ─► store (criteria)                user filters ─┐
store ─► effect reads the criteria                            ▼
effect ─► calls the back end                    the grid builds the request
effect ─► cancels the older call                the grid calls source.fetch(request)
effect ─► puts the rows in the store            the grid keeps the pages, the total,
store ─► the grid shows them                    the loading bar, the error and Retry

two copies of the same truth                    one place that knows
```

### The request, filled in as the user works

Each gesture fills one part of the request; the grid sends it whole, once per change.

```text
the user types « Ves » in Name's filter   ─►  request.filter  = { name: { type: 'text', op: 'contains', value: 'Ves' } }
the user sorts by Diameter, largest first ─►  request.sort    = [{ column: 'diameter', dir: 'desc' }]
the user goes to page 3                   ─►  request.page    = { index: 2, size: 100, offset: 200 }
your own values, from outside the grid    ─►  request.params  = { from: '2026-01-01', to: '2026-06-30' }
the grid, to cancel an older call         ─►  request.signal
```

### `params`: what comes from outside the grid

Say the page has an « observation window » picker **above** the grid, not a column filter. The window must reach the
back end with every request, and changing it must start again from page 1. That is what `params` is for:

```text
window picker (outside the grid) ──► window (a signal)
                                         │
                                         ▼
                         sourceRows(source, { params: { from, to } })
                                         │   the grid puts params into EVERY request
                                         ▼
                         source.fetch(request)        request.params = { from, to }
                                         │
                                         ▼
                         your translator ──► the body your back end expects:
                                             { seenAfter: from, seenBefore: to, …the column filters }
```

Two things to see in this picture:

1. `params` only **carries** the window to your code; **your translator** decides where it goes in the body.
2. A new `params` **tells the grid the question changed**: back to page 1, the older call cancelled, the selection
   cleared — on its own.

The tempting shortcut is to read the window straight from your translator. The request would be right, but the grid
would not know it changed: it would stay on page 5 and keep showing the old pages until something else moved.

### The translator: your back end keeps its own format

The grid sends filters in one well-defined shape; your back end may already speak another one. A small translator
sits between them, and the back end does not change:

```ts
import { sourceRows, type DataRequest, type DataResponse } from '@dzgrid/core/server';

type Asteroid = { id: string; name: string; found: string; diameter: number };
type Filter = NonNullable<DataRequest['filter']>[string];

/** The observatory's own format: one criterion per column, the operator in `op`. */
type Criterion = { op: string; value?: unknown; values?: readonly unknown[] };

function criterion(f: Filter): Criterion | null {
  switch (f.type) {
    case 'text': return { op: f.op, value: f.value };
    case 'number': return f.op === 'between' ? { op: 'range', values: [f.value, f.valueTo] } : { op: f.op, value: f.value };
    case 'day': return f.op === 'between' ? { op: 'range', values: [f.value, f.valueTo] } : { op: f.op, value: f.value };
    case 'set': return { op: 'in', values: f.include ?? [] };
    default: return null;
  }
}

/** The grid's request → the observatory's body (the window from `params` first, the user's filters over it). */
function body(req: DataRequest): Record<string, unknown> {
  const criteria: Record<string, Criterion> = {};
  const { from, to } = req.params as { from?: string; to?: string };
  if (from && to) criteria['found'] = { op: 'range', values: [from, to] };
  for (const [column, f] of Object.entries(req.filter ?? {})) {
    const c = criterion(f);
    if (c) criteria[column] = c;
  }
  const first = req.sort?.[0];
  return { criteria, orderBy: first?.column ?? null, order: first?.dir ?? null };
}

async function fetchPage(req: DataRequest): Promise<DataResponse<Asteroid>> {
  const answer = await fetch(`/api/catalogue?page=${req.page?.index ?? 0}&size=${req.page?.size ?? 100}`, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify(body(req)),
    signal: req.signal as AbortSignal,
  });
  const json = (await answer.json()) as { items: Asteroid[]; count: number };
  return { rows: json.items, total: json.count };
}

/** A new window = a new source with other params = a new question, from page 1. */
export const catalogue = (from: string, to: string) => sourceRows<Asteroid>({ fetch: fetchPage }, { params: { from, to } });
```

### Cancelling: only the latest answer counts

```text
the user types  V      Ve      Ves
requests        ──1──► ──2──►  ──3──►
                  ✕ cancelled (signal)
                         ✕ cancelled
answers                               ◄──3── shown
a late answer 2 that still arrives  ◄──2──  ignored: stale
```

Pass `request.signal` to your HTTP call so the network work stops too; the grid ignores a stale answer either way.

### The first screen, in one call

The default sort (newest first, say) and the starting window leave **with the very first request**: one round trip,
never « unsorted, then sorted ». Give the sort with `gridState({ initial: { v: 1, sort: [...] } })` (Angular:
`[state]`) and the window as `params` from the start.

### What the grid then does on its own

Loading, the thin « updating » bar, an error with Retry, the pages, stale answers, a selection that spans every page
(« all that match », sent as the query and the rows left out) — without a store, an effect or a cache of yours.

## Pages

```ts
import { createGrid, type GridMessages } from '@dzgrid/dom';
import { sourceRows, type DataRequest, type DataResponse } from '@dzgrid/core/server';
import { filters } from '@dzgrid/dom/filters-base';
import { pagination } from '@dzgrid/dom/pagination';
import { EN } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en';
import { EN_FILTERS } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en-filters';
import { EN_PAGINATION } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en-pagination';

type Asteroid = { id: string; name: string; found: string; diameter: number };

async function page(req: DataRequest): Promise<DataResponse<Asteroid>> {
  const answer = await fetch('/api/asteroids', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ filter: req.filter, quick: req.quick, sort: req.sort, page: req.page, zone: req.zone }),
    signal: req.signal as AbortSignal,
  });
  return answer.json();   // { rows, total }
}

const messages: GridMessages = { ...EN, text: { ...EN.text, ...EN_FILTERS.text, ...EN_PAGINATION.text } };

createGrid<Asteroid>(document.getElementById('asteroids')!, {
  source: sourceRows<Asteroid>({ fetch: page }, { params: { catalogue: 'made-up' } }),
  columns: [
    { id: 'name', header: 'Asteroid' },
    { id: 'found', header: 'Found', type: 'day' },
    { id: 'diameter', header: 'Diameter (km)', type: 'number' },
  ],
  getRowId: (a) => a.id,
  messages,
  operations: 'server',
  pagination: { pageSize: 100, pageSizes: [50, 100, 200] },
  features: [filters(), pagination()],
  onEvent: (e) => {
    if (e.type === 'fetchFailed') console.warn('the server did not answer', e.error);
  },
});
```

- The request: `filter` (in a wire form: days and instants already resolved in the grid's zone), `quick`, `sort`,
  `page` (`offset` and `size`, or a cursor with `paging: 'cursor'`), your `params`, the `zone`, a `key` naming the
  query, and a `signal`.
- The answer: `rows`, and `total` when known; without a total, `hasNext` says whether there is more.
- Only the answer to the latest request is shown, whatever order answers arrive in; older requests are aborted
  through `signal`. A failure shows an error with a retry button and a `fetchFailed` event.
- `operations` places each stage: `'server'` (the default with a source) sends filter, search, sort and page to the
  server; `{ filter: 'client', sort: 'client', page: 'off' }` asks for every row once and finishes in the browser. Server
  pages imply filter, search and sort on the server too.
- `refresh` (Angular `ctrl.refresh({})`, plain TypeScript `rows.refresh` command) asks again and keeps the rows shown
  meanwhile; the `busy` setting shows a thin bar while you reload.

## Infinite scroll

```ts
import { createGrid } from '@dzgrid/dom';
import { infiniteRows } from '@dzgrid/core/infinite';
import type { DataRequest } from '@dzgrid/core/server';
import { EN } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en';

type Star = { id: number; name: string; magnitude: number };

const stars = infiniteRows<Star>({
  fetch: async (req: DataRequest) => {
    const at = req.page?.offset ?? 0;
    const rows = Array.from({ length: 100 }, (_, i) => ({ id: at + i, name: `Star ${at + i}`, magnitude: (at + i) % 7 }));
    return { rows, total: 1_000_000 };
  },
}, { blockSize: 100, maxBlocks: 20 });

createGrid<Star>(document.getElementById('sky')!, {
  source: stars,
  columns: [{ id: 'name', header: 'Star' }, { id: 'magnitude', header: 'Magnitude', type: 'number' }],
  getRowId: (s) => s.id,
  messages: EN,
});
```

Blocks arrive while the user scrolls (`ahead` blocks in advance, `concurrency` at a time); at most `maxBlocks` are
kept. Rows not loaded yet show as loading rows; a failed block shows « retry » in its place. With an unknown total,
Ctrl+End goes to the last row known, and further each time it is pressed.

## Groups on the server

`serverSideRows(data, { by, aggFuncs })` sends one request per level: the request's `group` says which level and which
open path; the server answers that level's groups with their counts and totals, or a group's rows in blocks. The grid
computes no total itself. The [`server-side-groups.md`](https://github.com/plinthworks/dzgrid/blob/main/docs/behaviors/server-side-groups.md) sheet gives the request
and answer shapes; [pivot on a server](https://github.com/plinthworks/dzgrid/blob/main/docs/guide/pivot.md#pivot-on-a-server) builds on it.

## Rows that change

With `rows`, give a new array, or apply a transaction (rows are matched by id; the focus, selection and open rows stay):

```ts
import { createGrid } from '@dzgrid/dom';
import type { ClientModel } from '@dzgrid/core';
import { EN } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en';

type Buoy = { id: string; sea: string; wave: number };

const grid = createGrid<Buoy, ClientModel<Buoy>>(document.getElementById('buoys')!, {
  rows: [{ id: 'y1', sea: 'Glass sea', wave: 1.2 }],
  columns: [{ id: 'sea', header: 'Sea' }, { id: 'wave', header: 'Wave (m)', type: 'number' }],
  getRowId: (b) => b.id,
  messages: EN,
});

grid.kernel.rows.applyTransaction({ add: [{ id: 'y2', sea: 'Salt bay', wave: 0.4 }], patch: [{ id: 'y1', set: { wave: 2.8 } }] });
```

In Angular: `ctrl.applyTransaction(tx)` and `ctrl.applyTransactionAsync(tx)` (many small updates gathered into one).

---

<!-- docs/guide/row-moves.md -->

# Row moves

`rowDrag()` from `@dzgrid/dom/row-drag` lets the user move rows: drag the grip at the start of a cell, or press
Alt+Shift+↑ / ↓ (Option+Shift on a Mac), Alt+Shift+Home / End, and in a tree Alt+Shift+→ / ← to indent or outdent; or
use the right-click menu. Texts `-row-drag`, CSS `row-drag.css`. The grip takes mouse, pen and finger; the keys make
dragging never the only way.

The grid tells you where the rows go with a `rowMove` event; **your data decides**. `moveRows` from
`@dzgrid/core/row-drag` applies a move to your array (or tree of parent ids) and returns a new one.

```ts
import { createGrid, type GridMessages } from '@dzgrid/dom';
import { moveRows } from '@dzgrid/core/row-drag';
import { rowDrag } from '@dzgrid/dom/row-drag';
import { contextMenu } from '@dzgrid/dom/context-menu';
import { EN } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en';
import { EN_ROW_DRAG } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en-row-drag';
import { EN_CONTEXT_MENU } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en-context-menu';
import '@dzgrid/theme/dzgrid.css';
import '@dzgrid/theme/menu.css';
import '@dzgrid/theme/row-drag.css';

type Chore = { id: string; title: string; done: boolean };

let chores: Chore[] = [
  { id: 'c1', title: 'Wind the clock tower', done: false },
  { id: 'c2', title: 'Oil the weather vane', done: true },
  { id: 'c3', title: 'Count the pigeons', done: false },
];
const id = (c: Chore) => c.id;
const messages: GridMessages = { ...EN, text: { ...EN.text, ...EN_ROW_DRAG.text, ...EN_CONTEXT_MENU.text } };

const moves = rowDrag<Chore>({ column: 'title', canDrag: (c) => !c.done });
const grid = createGrid<Chore>(document.getElementById('chores')!, {
  rows: chores,
  columns: [{ id: 'title', header: 'Chore', flex: 1 }, { id: 'done', header: 'Done', type: 'boolean' }],
  getRowId: id,
  messages,
  selection: { mode: 'multi' },
  features: [moves, contextMenu<Chore>({ items: (c, defaults) => [...defaults, { separator: true }, ...moves.menuItems(c)] })],
  onEvent: (e) => {
    if (e.type === 'rowMove' && !e.applied) {
      chores = moveRows(chores, e, id);
      grid.update({ rows: chores });
    }
  },
});
```

- `apply: true` lets the grid reorder flat browser rows itself (the event then says `applied: true`); with a store
  (NgRx, signals) leave it off and apply the move where your state lives.
- The grip of a **selected** row drags every selected row shown.
- `canDrag(row)` and `canDrop({ keys, rows, target, parent })` refuse a move; `maxRows` caps how many rows move at once.
- While the rows are sorted or grouped, a move is refused and the grid says why; `whenSorted: 'allow'` sends the event
  anyway and lets you decide.
- With a server source the grid only sends the event (`apply` is ignored): save the new order on the server, then
  refresh.
- In a [tree](https://github.com/plinthworks/dzgrid/blob/main/docs/guide/tree.md), a row can be dropped inside another (`target.where: 'inside'`); `moveRows(rows, move, id, { parentId,
  setParent })` rewrites the parent ids for you.
- In Angular, the `(rowMove)` output carries the same event, and `ctrl.rowDrag()` the api (`move`, `step`).

## Between grids, or onto your own element

`moves.api(grid)?.dropTargets.add(element, { accept(keys), drop(keys) })` makes any element a place to drop rows: a
bin, a folder list, another grid's box. Moving rows from one grid to another is two updates of your own data: take
them out of one array and add them to the other.

---

<!-- docs/guide/dock-panels.md -->

# Dock and panels

Two panels come with DzGrid: the **columns chooser** (`columnsChooser()` from `@dzgrid/dom/columns-panel`: search,
show, hide and order columns; texts `-columns`, CSS `columns-panel.css`) and the **filters panel** (`filtersPanel()` from
`@dzgrid/dom/filters-panel`: every column's filter in one list; texts `-filters-panel`, CSS `filters-panel.css`).
Without a dock, the chooser opens as a dialog and the filters panel stands at its own side.

`dock()` from `@dzgrid/dom/dock` gives them, and panels of your own, a place beside or under the rows (texts `-dock`,
CSS `dock.css`): areas `start` and `end` (beside the rows, logical sides) and `bottom`. Each area can be resized by its
edge (also with the arrow keys), collapsed to a strip, closed, or moved to another area; two panels in one area become
tabs.

```ts
import { createGrid, type GridMessages } from '@dzgrid/dom';
import { dock } from '@dzgrid/dom/dock';
import { columnsChooser } from '@dzgrid/dom/columns-panel';
import { filtersPanel } from '@dzgrid/dom/filters-panel';
import { filters } from '@dzgrid/dom/filters-base';
import { columnMenu } from '@dzgrid/dom/column-menu';
import { EN } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en';
import { EN_DOCK } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en-dock';
import { EN_COLUMNS } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en-columns';
import { EN_FILTERS } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en-filters';
import { EN_FILTERS_PANEL } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en-filters-panel';
import { EN_COLUMN_MENU } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en-column-menu';
import '@dzgrid/theme/dzgrid.css';
import '@dzgrid/theme/dock.css';
import '@dzgrid/theme/columns-panel.css';
import '@dzgrid/theme/filters-panel.css';
import '@dzgrid/theme/menu.css';

type Potion = { id: string; name: string; colour: string; doses: number };

const messages: GridMessages = {
  ...EN,
  text: { ...EN.text, ...EN_DOCK.text, ...EN_COLUMNS.text, ...EN_FILTERS.text, ...EN_FILTERS_PANEL.text, ...EN_COLUMN_MENU.text },
};

const chooser = columnsChooser();
const panels = dock({
  open: { columns: 'end' },
  sizes: { min: 200, max: 480 },
  panels: [{
    id: 'notes',
    title: 'Notes',
    area: 'bottom',
    mount(host) {
      const p = host.ownerDocument.createElement('p');
      p.textContent = 'Shake before use.';
      host.append(p);
      return () => p.remove();
    },
  }],
  onChange: (layout) => console.log('dock moved', layout),
});

const grid = createGrid<Potion>(document.getElementById('potions')!, {
  rows: [{ id: 'p1', name: 'Fog in a bottle', colour: 'grey', doses: 3 }],
  columns: [{ id: 'name', header: 'Potion' }, { id: 'colour', header: 'Colour' }, { id: 'doses', header: 'Doses', type: 'number' }],
  getRowId: (p) => p.id,
  messages,
  features: [filters(), chooser, filtersPanel(), columnMenu({ use: { chooser } }), panels],
});

panels.api(grid)?.show('notes');
panels.api(grid)?.move('filters', 'start');
```

- The panels' ids: `columns` (the chooser), `filters` (the filters panel), and the ids of your own panels.
- `open: { id: area }` shows a panel there at the start; otherwise the chooser waits at the end until opened (the
  column menu's « Choose columns », or `chooser.api(grid)?.open()`), and your panels wait at their `area` (`end` by
  default) until `api.show(id)`.
- Your panel's `mount(host)` builds its content and may return a cleanup function.
- `api`: `show`, `hide`, `move`, `collapse`, `resize`, `layout()`, `setLayout(layout)`. With the [state](https://github.com/plinthworks/dzgrid/blob/main/docs/guide/state.md)
  feature, where each panel stands is saved with the rest of the grid's state.
- A floating window (area `float`) is planned, not there yet: it is refused with a warning.

---

<!-- docs/guide/export-print.md -->

# Export and print

## CSV and Excel

`csvExport({ canExport })` from `@dzgrid/dom/export` writes the grid's rows to a CSV file, and to an Excel file
(`.xlsx`) with `xlsx: true` (texts `-export`). The file holds the visible columns in their order, the sort and the
filters; values are written as values (ISO days, instants in the grid's zone, numbers a spreadsheet can add up), or as
the cells show them with `text: 'display'`.

```ts
import { createGrid, type GridMessages } from '@dzgrid/dom';
import { csvExport } from '@dzgrid/dom/export';
import { EN } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en';
import { EN_EXPORT } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en-export';

type Kettle = { id: string; model: string; litres: number; boughtOn: string };

const exporter = csvExport({
  canExport: true,
  xlsx: true,
  separator: ';',
  fileName: ({ scope }) => `kettles-${scope}`,
});
const messages: GridMessages = { ...EN, text: { ...EN.text, ...EN_EXPORT.text } };

createGrid<Kettle>(document.getElementById('kettles')!, {
  rows: [{ id: 'k1', model: 'Whistling Wren', litres: 1.7, boughtOn: '2024-12-01' }],
  columns: [
    { id: 'model', header: 'Model' },
    { id: 'litres', header: 'Litres', type: 'number' },
    { id: 'boughtOn', header: 'Bought on', type: 'day' },
  ],
  getRowId: (k) => k.id,
  messages,
  selection: { mode: 'multi' },
  features: [exporter],
});

exporter.bind(document.getElementById('csv')!, { scope: 'displayed' });
exporter.bind(document.getElementById('xlsx')!, { scope: 'displayed', format: 'xlsx' });
document.getElementById('selected')!.addEventListener('click', async () => {
  const outcome = await exporter.run('selected');   // 'done' | 'refused' | 'failed' | 'cancelled' | 'busy'
  console.log(outcome);
});
```

- Scopes: `'displayed'` (the rows shown now: the current page when paged), `'selected'`, `'all'` (every row the
  query matches, on every page; the filters still apply).
- `canExport: true`, or a function that may refuse (`{ ok: false, reason }`) — a place for your own permission rule.
- A text starting like a formula (`=`, `+`, `-`, `@`) gets a leading `'` so a spreadsheet does not run it; a number
  such as `-5` never does. `numbers: 'excel'` (the default) writes the locale's decimal mark when the separator is `;`,
  `numbers: 'raw'` the machine form. `csv: 'text'` on a column keeps identifiers such as `0123` as text.
- The file is built in chunks so the page never freezes; `exporter.cancel()` stops it, `onProgress` follows it.
- With server data, the grid holds only some rows: give `exportAll(request, { signal, progress })`, which asks your
  server for the file (the request carries the query in wire form) and returns `{ url }` or `{ blob }`.
- The right-click menu offers the same: `contextMenu({ use: { csv: exporter, xlsx: exporter.xlsx } })`.
- In Angular: `<button [dzgExport]="exporter" dzgExportScope="displayed">` (directive `DzgExport`).

## Print

`print(grid, { title })` from `@dzgrid/dom/print` prints the rows as they are on screen — same columns, order, sort and
filters, not only the rows scrolled into view — as a real table: headers repeated on each page, no row cut in two,
right to left in Arabic, a dark theme printed light (texts `-print`, CSS `print.css`). At most 5 000 rows (`maxRows`);
beyond, a line says how many were printed. A grid with server pages prints the page shown.

```ts
import { createGrid, type GridMessages } from '@dzgrid/dom';
import { print } from '@dzgrid/dom/print';
```
