```ts
import { printOnMenu } from '@dzgrid/dom/print-menu';
import { EN } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en';
import { EN_PRINT } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en-print';
import '@dzgrid/theme/dzgrid.css';
import '@dzgrid/theme/print.css';

type Bell = { id: string; tower: string; note: string };

const messages: GridMessages = { ...EN, text: { ...EN.text, ...EN_PRINT.text } };
const grid = createGrid<Bell>(document.getElementById('bells')!, {
  rows: [{ id: 'b1', tower: 'Saltmarsh', note: 'F sharp' }],
  columns: [{ id: 'tower', header: 'Tower' }, { id: 'note', header: 'Note' }],
  getRowId: (b) => b.id,
  messages,
});

document.getElementById('print')!.addEventListener('click', () => void print(grid, { title: 'Bells of the coast' }));
printOnMenu(grid, { title: 'Bells of the coast' });   // the browser's own Ctrl+P prints the whole grid too
```

`print` is a function, not a feature: nothing is loaded until it is called. `printOnMenu(grid)` makes the browser's
own print command (Ctrl+P, the File menu) print the whole grid as well; without it, that command prints only what the
page shows. In Angular, pass `ctrl.grid()` to both.

---

<!-- docs/guide/state.md -->

# State

`gridState()` from `@dzgrid/dom/state` reads and restores the grid's state: the columns (order, width, hidden,
pinned), header groups, sort, filters, quick search, page and page size, density, grouped columns, the dock's layout,
the pivot. A state is a plain, versioned object (`{ v: 1, … }`) you can store anywhere. It never holds row data, but it does
hold what the user typed into filters.

```ts
import { createGrid } from '@dzgrid/dom';
import { gridState, type GridState } from '@dzgrid/dom/state';
import { EN } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/en';

type Lantern = { id: string; street: string; lit: boolean; height: number };

const state = gridState({
  initial: { v: 1, sort: [{ column: 'street', dir: 'asc' }] },
  persist: { key: 'lanterns-grid' },
  debounce: 300,
});

const grid = createGrid<Lantern>(document.getElementById('lanterns')!, {
  rows: [{ id: 'l1', street: 'Wick lane', lit: true, height: 3.5 }],
  columns: [
    { id: 'street', header: 'Street' },
    { id: 'lit', header: 'Lit', type: 'boolean' },
    { id: 'height', header: 'Height (m)', type: 'number' },
  ],
  getRowId: (l) => l.id,
  messages: EN,
  features: [state],
  onEvent: (e) => {
    if (e.type === 'stateChanged') save(e.state);
  },
});

function save(s: GridState) { console.log(JSON.stringify(s)); }

const api = state.api(grid);
const saved = api?.state();
if (saved) api?.setState(saved);   // returns the problems of a state it could not fully read
api?.reset();                      // back to the columns and options the grid was made with
```

- `initial` is applied before the first paint, and on a server before the first request: one request at start.
- `persist: { key, include? }` keeps the state in `localStorage` under that key and restores it at start; blocked or
  full storage throws nothing (one `state-storage` warning). `persistLocal(grid, key)` does the same for a grid made
  without the option.
- `stateChanged` comes after a pause (`debounce`, 300 ms) following a user's change: a resized column, a sort, a
  filter, a panel moved.
- A restore never throws. Unknown or removed column ids are skipped (warning `state-column`), columns the state does
  not name keep their settings and go after the named ones, a field of the wrong type is skipped; a state written by
  a newer version (`v` higher) is refused whole (`state-version`).
- Not saved: open rows, the selection, the focus, the scroll position, edits in progress.

## In the address

`toSearchParams(state)` and `fromSearchParams(params)` write the state as one compact parameter (`?grid=1.…`) and read
it back. Typed filter values and the search may be names or record numbers, and an address reaches the browser
history, server logs and `Referer` headers: they are left out unless you ask with `include: ['filter', 'quick']`.

```ts
import { toSearchParams, fromSearchParams, type GridState } from '@dzgrid/dom/state';

export function writeAddress(state: GridState): void {
  const { params } = toSearchParams(state, { name: 'grid' });
  history.replaceState(null, '', `?${params.toString()}`);
}

export function readAddress(): GridState | null {
  return fromSearchParams(new URLSearchParams(location.search), { name: 'grid' }).state;
}
```

The helpers never touch `history` themselves: you choose `pushState` or `replaceState`. In Angular, `[state]` restores
a state, `(stateChanged)` hears it, and `ctrl.resetState()` resets.

---

<!-- docs/guide/theming-rtl.md -->

# Theming and right to left

## The theme

`@dzgrid/dom` injects the grid's layout CSS by itself; `@dzgrid/theme` makes it presentable (colours, lines, header,
hover, selection, focus, popups), light and dark, checked for contrast. Each feature with a look has its own sheet,
loaded after `dzgrid.css`: `columns.css`, `menu.css`, `grouping.css`, `pivot.css`, `edit.css`, `range.css`,
`fill.css`, `dock.css`, `columns-panel.css`, `filters-panel.css`, `find.css`, `search.css`, `print.css`,
`row-drag.css`, `pinned-rows.css`, `row-numbers.css`, `fresh-rows.css`.

```ts
import '@dzgrid/theme/dzgrid.css';
import '@dzgrid/theme/menu.css';
import '@dzgrid/theme/contrast.css';   // more contrast when the system asks for it
```

- **Cascade layer.** Every rule sits in the layer `dzgrid`: your own classes win without `!important`. When you layer
  your own CSS, name the order once, first: `@layer theme, base, dzgrid, components, utilities;`. With an unlayered
  reset (Tailwind 3's preflight, Bootstrap's Reboot), load the `*.unlayered.css` copies instead.
- **Bridges.** `tailwind.css` (Tailwind 4), `tailwind3.css`, `bootstrap.css` (5.3, follows `data-bs-theme`) map the
  grid's colours, font and corners to your framework's.
- **Showcase themes.** `midnight.css` and `clinic.css`, each with a light and a dark twin; `data-dzg-skin="midnight"`
  on a container styles only that area.

## Colours and sizes

Colours are CSS variables only. The palette (shared with tzslot), each a `light-dark()` pair on `:root`: `--tz-bg`,
`--tz-bg-raised`, `--tz-fg`, `--tz-fg-muted`, `--tz-border`, `--tz-accent`, `--tz-accent-fg`, `--tz-danger`,
`--tz-warning`, `--tz-success`. What the grid derives, set on any ancestor of `.dzg`: `--dzg-font`, `--dzg-radius`,
`--dzg-cell-padding-inline`, `--dzg-header-bg`, `--dzg-row-hover-bg`, `--dzg-row-selected-bg`, `--dzg-focus-ring`,
`--dzg-line`, `--dzg-pill-radius`, `--dzg-header-size`, `--dzg-select-bar`, `--dzg-flash`, `--dzg-flash-color`.

```css
:root { --tz-accent: light-dark(#7c3aed, #c4b5fd); }
.dzg { --dzg-radius: 6px; --dzg-font: "Atkinson Hyperlegible", system-ui, sans-serif; }
.dzg-cell.is-late { color: var(--tz-danger); }
```

**Light and dark** follow the system; `data-theme="light"` or `data-theme="dark"` on any ancestor forces one.

**Row height** comes from the `density` setting (`compact` 28 px, `comfortable` 32 px, the default, `spacious` 40 px)
or `rowHeight` in pixels, which wins. Rows follow the reader's text zoom. The column menu can offer the density to the
user (`columnMenu({ density: true })`), and the [state](https://github.com/plinthworks/dzgrid/blob/main/docs/guide/state.md) keeps it.

## Right to left

Direction is designed in: pinned columns, scrolling, the arrow keys (in Arabic, → moves toward the start, which is on the right), popups, the
tree's indent and the theme all follow it. Everything in DzGrid speaks of **start** and **end**, never left and right:
`pinned: 'start'`, `align: 'end'`, the dock's `start` area.

```ts
import { createGrid } from '@dzgrid/dom';
import { AR } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/ar';

type Souk = { id: string; name: string; stalls: number };

const grid = createGrid<Souk>(document.getElementById('souks')!, {
  rows: [{ id: 's1', name: 'سوق النجوم', stalls: 48 }],
  columns: [
    { id: 'name', header: 'السوق', pinned: 'start' },
    { id: 'stalls', header: 'الدكاكين', type: 'number', align: 'end' },
  ],
  getRowId: (s) => s.id,
  messages: AR,
  locale: 'ar-DZ',
  direction: 'rtl',
  numerals: 'locale',
});

grid.update({ direction: 'auto' });   // follow the nearest `dir` attribute instead
```

- `direction`: `'ltr'`, `'rtl'`, or `'auto'` (the nearest ancestor's `dir`).
- `numerals: 'locale'` shows the language's own digits (Arabic-Indic for `ar`); the default `'latn'` keeps 0–9.
- Sorting and searching follow the language: hamza forms, short vowels and tatweel, Arabic-Indic digits.
- Your own CSS should use logical properties as well: `margin-inline-start`, `inset-inline-end`, `text-align: start`.
- Three languages ship: `EN`, `FR`, `AR` (`@dzgrid/dom/locales/*`), each feature with its own bundle, plural rules
  included. Another language is a `GridMessages` object of your own with the same keys; `checkMessages(messages)` throws,
  naming the keys that are missing.

---

<!-- docs/guide/accessibility.md -->

# Accessibility

DzGrid follows the WAI-ARIA grid pattern (a treegrid for trees and groups) and aims at WCAG 2.2 AA. The draft
conformance report is [`docs/a11y/acr-wcag22.md`](https://github.com/plinthworks/dzgrid/blob/main/docs/a11y/acr-wcag22.md): it says, criterion by criterion, what is
checked and how. Its screen-reader listening is not done yet, so the criteria that rest on what a screen reader says
are marked « partially supports » until then.

## What the grid does

- **One tab stop.** Tab enters the grid at the focused cell; the arrows, Page Up / Down, Home / End and Ctrl+Home /
  End move inside; Tab leaves. The focus is never lost when rows are sorted, filtered, reloaded or scrolled away
  (rows are virtualised: the focused row is kept).
- **Roles and states.** `role="grid"` (or `treegrid`), real row and column counts (`aria-rowcount`, `aria-colcount`)
  even when only some rows are drawn, `aria-sort` on sorted headers, `aria-selected` and `aria-expanded` on rows,
  `aria-readonly` where editing is on.
- **Announcements.** Sorting, filtering, a page change, an export, a refused edit, a row moved are said through a live
  region, in the grid's language, with plurals.
- **Every action has a keyboard way**: column moves and sizes, row moves (Alt+Shift+arrows), the fill (Ctrl+D /
  Ctrl+R), the dock's edges and tabs, the menus (Shift+F10 or the Menu key). Dragging is never the only way.
- **Targets** of 24 px at least; **contrast** of 4.5:1 for every text and 3:1 for every part, checked by script on
  every colour pair, light and dark; **forced colours** (Windows High Contrast) use the system's colours; motion
  follows `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- **Zoom and text size.** Page zoom to 400 % works; at 320 CSS pixels wide nothing scrolls sideways outside the
  grid; rows grow with the reader's default text size.

## What is left to you

- **A name.** Give the `label` setting (`label="Invoices"`, `[label]` in Angular), or every grid on the page has the same generic
  name (« Data grid »).
- **Translated texts.** Headers are your strings, already in the user's language; the grid's own sentences come from
  `messages` (English, French and Arabic ship). A part's own texts go through its context's `msg('app.key')`.
- **The page's language and direction** (`lang` and `dir` on `<html>`): the grid follows `direction: 'auto'` and
  says its sentences in its `messages`' language.
- **Custom parts keep their promises.** A cell part draws inside a cell the grid owns (role, focus, keys stay the
  grid's); a button in it must be a real `<button type="button">` with a name. Do not move the focus yourself from a
  part; say things with the context's `announce(text)`.
- **Colours** only through the theme's variables (`--tz-*`, `--dzg-*`), so the contrast checks and the dark and
  forced-colours modes keep working. Do not convey meaning by colour alone: a `badge` part writes its text too.
- **Problems.** A `Problem` never carries row data (rows may be personal), only a code, a path and a short detail:
  log them, do not show them to the user as they are.

```ts
import { createGrid } from '@dzgrid/dom';
import { FR } from '@dzgrid/dom/locales/fr';

type Phare = { id: string; nom: string; portee: number };

document.documentElement.lang = 'fr';
document.documentElement.dir = 'ltr';

const grid = createGrid<Phare>(document.getElementById('phares')!, {
  rows: [{ id: 'p1', nom: 'Phare des Brumes', portee: 22 }],
  columns: [{ id: 'nom', header: 'Phare' }, { id: 'portee', header: 'Portée (milles)', type: 'number' }],
  getRowId: (p) => p.id,
  messages: FR,
  locale: 'fr-FR',
  label: 'Phares de la côte',
  direction: 'auto',
});

grid.api.announce('Liste mise à jour');
```

The owner's hand-made listening route (keyboard and screen readers, the essential path) is
[`docs/a11y/parcours-essentiel.md`](https://github.com/plinthworks/dzgrid/blob/main/docs/a11y/parcours-essentiel.md).
